skills.title: The skills
skills.sub: Each skill is a standard folder with a SKILL.md — the instructions an agent reads — plus a small Python tool. Nothing to sign up for.
gp.tagline: All your work on a GitHub Project board
gp.desc: Talk to your agent in plain words and it manages your GitHub Project board with the gh CLI — then reads the result back to confirm.
gp.f1: Issues: create, edit, move between columns, close, reopen, comment
gp.f2: Kanban columns: add, rename (cards stay), reorder, colour
gp.f3: Screenshots and videos attached to issues
gp.f4: TODO checklists inside an issue, with progress
gp.f6: A board per project with /gp init <board URL>
gp.t4: “Add a column Urgent at the front”
gp.req: Needs a free GitHub account, the gh CLI and Python 3.8+.
cs.tagline: Learn Claude Code and get better at it
cs.desc: Claude Code ships a new version almost every day. This skill teaches it in order, answers from the current official docs, checks your setup and summarizes every new feature.
cs.f1: 14 lessons with an exercise in your own project and check questions
cs.f3: Answers checked against the official docs, with the link
cs.f4: Every new CHANGELOG feature, summarized by topic
cs.f5: A setup doctor for settings, CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins and MCP
cs.f6: /claude-skill update pulls newly released features into the skill
cs.t2: “How do I run prettier after every edit with a hook?”
cs.req: Needs Python 3.8+ and internet access (it reads the official docs).

faq.title: Questions
faq.a1: A folder with a SKILL.md file that tells an AI agent when and how to do a task, plus the scripts and notes it needs. It is an open standard (agentskills.io), so the same folder works in many agents.
faq.q2: Every project or this project only?
faq.a2: “Every project” installs the skill once for all projects on your computer. “This project only” keeps it inside one repository; with the Claude Code plugin it is written to .claude/settings.json, so teammates get it too.
faq.q3: Why is the plugin called cc-skill and not claude-skill?
faq.a3: Claude Code reserves plugin names that start with claude- for Anthropic. The plugin is cc-skill; the skill inside keeps its name, so you still type /claude-skill.
faq.q4: Is it free? Where does my data go?
faq.a4: Free and MIT-licensed. The skills run on your computer with your own tools: gp talks only to GitHub through your gh login, and claude-skill reads the public Claude Code docs and CHANGELOG.
faq.q5: It doesn't show up after installing. What now?
faq.a5: In Claude Code, run /reload-plugins in the open chat or start a new one. In other agents, start a new session so the skill folder is read again. You can also just ask your agent: “is the gp skill installed?”

prompt.intro: Install the {skill} skill from the thruthesky/sonub-skills repository, {scope}.
prompt.what: It is a standard Agent Skill (a folder with SKILL.md): {url}
prompt.plugin: Install it as a Claude Code plugin. Run these in order (ignore “already added” errors):
prompt.already: If it is already installed, run this instead: {cmd}
prompt.doctor: Run {cmd} and fix whatever it reports.
prompt.doctorGp: Run {cmd} and fix whatever it reports (install gh, gh auth login, gh auth refresh -s project,repo).
prompt.report: Tell me briefly what was installed, the doctor result, and what I can say to start using it.
note.reload: Already in a Claude Code chat? Run /reload-plugins after installing from the terminal (or restart).
note.inChat: Inside a chat you can also type /plugin install {plugin}@sonub-skills and pick the scope on screen.
note.project: Run it inside your project folder.
note.teamShared: With --scope project it is written to .claude/settings.json — commit it and teammates get the skill too.
note.folderUpdate: Run the same line again to update. Delete {path} to remove.
note.newSession: Start a new session of your agent so it reads the new skill.
note.reqGp: Needs Python 3.8+ and the GitHub CLI gh.
start.gp1: Set it up: {cmd} — it checks gh and your GitHub login.
start.gp3: Then just talk: “make an issue: the login button does nothing on iPhone”, “move it to Done”.
